result.text:
有在用 Android、Termux 和 Flutter 的看過來。

這是我基於 termux-flutter 持續整理、自己也在用的版本：termux-flutter-wsl。

為什麼不能直接下載 Flutter 官方 Linux SDK 丟進 Termux？

因為一般 Linux 發行版主要使用 glibc，但 Android／Termux 的底層是 bionic libc。兩邊不只 C 函式庫不同，dynamic linker 路徑、系統呼叫封裝與工具鏈環境也不一樣，所以官方以 glibc 為 host 編譯的 Flutter、Dart 和 Engine binary，不能直接在 Android bionic 環境執行。

這個專案就是把 Flutter Engine、Dart runtime 與相關工具鏈針對 Android bionic／ARM64 重新編譯、打包和修補。

裝好後可以直接在 Termux 裡：

・執行 "flutter doctor"、"flutter create"
・編譯 Android APK
・編譯 Linux desktop
・搭配 Termux:X11 執行 "flutter run"
・直接使用 Hot Reload

目前已更新到 Flutter 3.44.2／Dart 3.12.1，提供 ".deb" 和一鍵安裝腳本，也跑過 Android 16 實機 smoke test。

名字裡的 WSL 是用來交叉編譯 Flutter SDK 與 Engine；一般使用者直接在 Termux 安裝 release 就能用，不需要自己重編整套工具鏈。

拿平板、折疊機，再接個鍵盤，就能直接變成一台隨身 Flutter 開發機。臨時改 code、跑專案，甚至直接在 Android 裝置上 build APK，都不用回到電腦。

目前主要支援 ARM64，本機 APK／sideload 開發流程最穩；API 35+ 與 AAB 發版仍屬實驗性。

result.text:
People of earth, its time to switch completely to building UIs with @rive_app.

​We’re running the entire file editor UI straight through Rive (with the file explorer still in progress). It’s not just rendering visual assets. Rive is actively handling data, pushing database updates, and driving motion directly to Flutter.

​Navigation feels instant. You trust every click, react without delay, and know with 100% certainty when an element is triggered, it’s the kind of effortless feel that eliminates software fatigue entirely.

​To lock in peak performance, we strategically balance the load: some Rive lists are populated by Flutter, while others run on Rive's own list property.

​The workflow upgrade is massive: jump into the rive editor, tweak the UI visually, export, hot reload and you’re good to go. Building UI hasn't felt this seamless ever.

result.text:
Why I chose Flutter over React Native in 2026:

• Single codebase → Android + iOS (not "sort of" — actually)
• Hot reload is faster than RN
• Dart is simpler than JavaScript for mobile
• Widget system is more predictable than JSX + native bridges
• Google is all-in (Gemini, Antigravity, Genkit Dart)

The tradeoff: smaller community, fewer third-party packages.
Worth it for solo devs who want ONE codebase that actually works on both platforms.

Flutter or React Native — what's your pick?
